prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 12 of 26 earlier cases, t = 0 in 14; when indemnified t per unit about 81 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per unit: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34)
- line 6 "Installer hours": no earlier line of this grade; level of the other hourly grades; when indemnified t per hr about 63 (80% range 23 to 176)
- line 8 "Service technician hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 47 (80% range 36 to 69); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), so this line (9 hr) about 425 (327 to 621)
- line 9 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 12 of 26 earlier cases, t = 0 in 14; when indemnified t per pc about 81 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34)
- line 15 "Service technician hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 47 (80% range 36 to 69); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), so this line (9 hr) about 425 (327 to 621)

items.description: Painting the disturbed wall area and closing the wall opening
items.rationale: Repair of the affected wall area after a covered escape of water event is indemnified under 7.1.5 and 7.1.7. Only the disturbed area is covered, not the whole room. Reference cases (e.g., Case 36, cleaning and repainting of affected areas) suggest similar work is indemnified.
Policy 7.1.7(f) allows one travel/call-out charge per contractor per invoice. Vehicle costs are indemnified in about half of prior cases, and this is the first such charge on this invoice.
Consumable installation material used in the repair of the affected pipe is covered under 7.1.7(c). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34) show such materials are indemnified if used for the repair.
Replacement pipe for the failed cold water line is covered as a necessary repair material under 7.1.7(c). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34, copper pipe repair) support this.
Replacement of insulation removed to access and repair the affected pipe is covered under 7.1.7(c). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34) support this.
Labour for pipe repair is covered under 7.1.7(g). No direct reference for 'installer' grade, but similar grades (see price priors) suggest about 63 per hour.

If used for leak detection or confirming repair, a flat-rate device charge is covered once per drying/repair operation under 7.1.7(e). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34, measurement technician) support this.
Labour for leak detection, repair, and drying is covered under 7.1.7(g). Price priors and reference cases (e.g., Case 21) suggest about 47 per hour, so 9 hrs ≈ 425.
Policy 7.1.7(f) allows one travel/call-out charge per contractor per invoice. This is the first such charge for this contractor.
Drying of the affected area is necessary after a water leak and is covered under 7.1.7(b) and (e). Reference cases (e.g., Case 36, drying unit rental) suggest a typical threshold of 58–84.
Consumable installation material used in the repair is covered under 7.1.7(c), provided it is not a reusable tool. Reference cases (e.g., Case 34) support this.
If these are pipe fittings or connectors used in the repair, they are covered under 7.1.7(c). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34) support this.
If both lengths were needed for the repair of the affected pipe, both are covered under 7.1.7(c). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34) support this.
Replacement insulation for the repaired pipe is covered under 7.1.7(c). Reference cases (e.g., Case 34) support this.
If this is not a duplicate charge for the same work, but for additional necessary repair/drying work, it is covered under 7.1.7(g). Price priors and reference cases suggest about 425 for 9 hrs.
